title: L8 · Skull
subtitle: Bone markings, cranial and facial bones, sinuses

lines.text: Bone markings show where muscles attach and where nerves pass.
A **trochanter** is a very large blunt projection. It's only on the femur.
A spine is sharp. A **process** is any projection.
A **tuberosity** is large and rough. A **tubercle** is small and smooth.
An epicondyle sits above a condyle.

scenes.title: Bone markings: openings and joint surfaces

lines.text: Openings let vessels and nerves through.
A notch is on an edge. A **foramen** is a round hole.
A **meatus** is a tunnel. A fissure is a slit.
A **condyle** is a round joint surface. A facet is flat.
A **fossa** is a shallow basin. A **sinus** is an air-filled cavity.
The **frontal** bone is the forehead. It holds the frontal sinus.
The two **parietal** bones form the top sides of the head.
The **coronal suture** joins the frontal and parietal bones.
The **sagittal suture** joins the two parietals, right down the top.
The temporal bones are the lower sides, under the ears.
The **squamosal suture** joins temporal and parietal.
The **external auditory meatus**, or **EAM**, is the ear hole.
The **mastoid** process is the big bump behind the ear.
The **styloid** process is the sharp point in front of it.
The zygomatic process anchors the chewing muscles.
The occipital bone is the base of the skull.
The **lambdoid suture** joins it to the parietals.
The **foramen magnum**, the great hole, lets the spinal cord through.
The **occipital condyles** form a joint with the atlas.
The **EOP** is the midline bump where neck muscles attach.
The **sphenoid** is shaped like a bat or butterfly.
Its **sella turcica**, the Turkish saddle, holds the pituitary gland.
The **ethmoid** sits in front of it, in the roof of the nose.
Its crista galli anchors the brain's coverings.
Its **cribriform plate** is full of holes for the smell nerves.
The superior and middle nasal conchae belong to the ethmoid.
The **maxillary** bones hold the upper teeth and the maxillary sinus.
The **nasal** bones form the bridge of the nose.
The **zygomatic** bones are the cheekbones.
With the temporal bone, they form the zygomatic arch.
The **lacrimal** bones sit on the inner wall of each orbit.
The **vomer** is a single bone. It forms the lower nasal septum.
The **palatine** bones form the back third of the hard palate.
The **inferior nasal conchae** form part of the nasal walls.
The mandible is the only movable bone of the skull.
Its condyle meets the temporal bone at the **TMJ**, the temporomandibular joint.
The **coronoid** process is in front of the condyle. The mandibular notch is between them.
The **ramus** runs up. The angle is where it turns. The body is the chin.
The alveolar process holds the teeth. The **mental foramina** are holes in the chin.
The paranasal sinuses warm, humidify and filter air.
They also make the skull lighter.
There are four pairs. FEMS.
**Frontal**, **ethmoid**, **maxillary**, **sphenoid**.

scenes.title: The hyoid and the ear ossicles

lines.text: The **hyoid** sits under the tongue.
It is the only bone that doesn't join another bone.
Each ear has three auditory ossicles, the smallest bones in the body.
The **malleus** is the hammer. The **incus** is the anvil. The **stapes** is the stirrup.
